recipes.title: Chimichurri Sauce
ingredients: 1 Fresno chile or red jalapeño, finely chopped
3-4 garlic cloves, thinly sliced or finely chopped
1 tsp. Diamond Crystal kosher salt (or 1/2 tsp. Morton), plus more
1/2 cup finely chopped fresh cilantro (leaves and tender stems)
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley (leaves and tender stems)
2 Tbsp. finely chopped fresh oregano leaves
steps: Combine shallot, chile, garlic, vinegar, and salt in a medium bowl. Let sit 10 minutes.
Stir in cilantro, parsley, and oregano.
Whisk in the olive oil.
Transfer 1/2 cup chimichurri to a small bowl; season with salt and reserve as sauce.
Optional marinade: toss remaining chimichurri with beef, chicken, or pork. Cover and chill at least 3 hours or overnight, then grill and spoon reserved chimichurri over the meat.
recipes.servings: About 1½ cups — roughly 8 servings as a sauce (estimated, BA's stated yield wasn't visible)

steps: Blend all ingredients into a grainy dough that holds its shape when you squeeze a handful.
Transfer onto a lined dehydrator tray or baking sheet.
Bake at 350°F for 30 minutes, flipping halfway through.
Alternative: dehydrate at 130°F for 8 hours instead of baking.
recipes.servings: Makes about 20-24 crackers (~6 servings, estimated — not stated in the original post)

recipes.title: Ground Venison Jerky
steps: Grind the venison, bacon, and apples (first on coarse, then on fine).
Mix in the rest of the ingredients.
Cover and refrigerate for 24-48 hours.
Load the jerky gun and press the mixture directly onto dehydrator trays.
Dehydrate at 160°F until dry (roughly 4-5 hours, varies by dehydrator).
Store in the fridge for 3-4 weeks, or freeze for up to 1 year.
recipes.servings: Makes roughly 3-4 lbs finished jerky — about 50 snack-sized servings (rough estimate; yield depends on moisture loss)

recipes.title: Parmesan-Crusted Butter Beans
ingredients: 1 (15-ounce) can butter beans, drained and rinsed
Extra-virgin olive oil (about 2 tablespoons, used in the cheese mixture)
steps: Position a rack in the center of the oven and preheat to 400°F. Line a quarter-sheet pan with parchment paper.
Transfer the butter beans to a cutting board and pat dry.
In a small bowl, combine the Parmesan, rosemary, chili paste, and 2 tablespoons oil; mix to combine.
Scatter the cheese mixture in a thick, even layer across the lined sheet pan. Layer the butter beans on top, making sure none overlap.
Bake until the cheese is golden brown and crisp, 40 to 45 minutes. Remove from the oven and let cool to room temperature.
Carefully slide the beans off the parchment paper, slice into big chunks, and serve.

ingredients: Roasted garlic cloves (amount not specified by source)
1 1/3 cups water reserved from boiling the kale
Black pepper, chili, and sesame seeds, for garnish (amounts not specified by source)

Blend until smooth and creamy (implied by the source's description; exact blend time not stated).
Spiralize the zucchini into noodles.
Combine the kale sauce with the zucchini noodles.

recipes.title: Spinach Potato Cakes with Cheese
ingredients: 1 tbsp olive oil, plus more for frying
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C/400°F.
Wrap the potato in foil and bake for 45 minutes, until fully softened.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the spinach until wilted.
Peel and mash the potato, then mix thoroughly with the spinach, garlic, nutritional yeast, garlic powder, salt, and flour.
On a floured surface, shape about 1/4 cup of the mixture into a flat circle.
Place about 1 teaspoon of dairy-free butter and 1 tablespoon of dairy-free cheese in the middle, then fold the edges together to form the potato cake shape.
Fry the potato cakes in olive oil for 3-4 minutes, then flip and fry 1-2 minutes more, until crispy.
recipes.servings: About 4 servings (roughly 10-12 potato cakes; estimated, not stated by source)

Shape the mixture into 16 balls, each about 1 inch in diameter.

recipes.title: Quick Pickled Red Onions
ingredients: 3/4 cup (180 ml) apple cider vinegar or distilled white vinegar
1 tsp kosher, sea, or pink Himalayan salt
Optional add-ins: 3-5 cloves garlic, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 chopped jalapeño, or 1-2 tsp fresh herbs
steps: Slice the onion into half or quarter-sized rings (a mandoline gives even thickness). Break up the slices and stuff them into a quart-sized glass mason jar.
Prepare the pickling liquid: add the vinegar, water, salt, sugar, and black peppercorns to a small pot over high heat, stirring to dissolve the salt and sugar.

Once the liquid boils, carefully pour it into the jar and let it sit on the counter until it cools to room temperature. Press down any onion pieces sticking above the liquid with a fork after 5-10 minutes.
Seal the jar and store in the fridge for up to one month. Most crisp within the first week, gradually softening with time.

recipes.title: 15-Minute Dairy-Free Mac & Cheese
steps: Boil the pasta: cook the macaroni in boiling water until al dente, then drain.
Mix the sauce: in a pan over medium heat, whisk together the coconut milk, hummus, nutritional yeast, smoked paprika, and LAND seasoning until smooth and warm.
Combine: toss the cooked macaroni into the sauce until well coated.
Crisp the topping: toast the panko in a separate pan with the olive oil until golden brown.
Serve: plate the mac and cheese and top with the crispy panko.

recipes.title: Butternut Squash Grilled Cheese with Pickled Fennel
ingredients: 1 small fennel bulb, stalks and fronds removed, thinly sliced
1 small butternut squash (1 1/2 pounds), halved and seeded
3 tablespoons salted butter, plus more for grilling the sandwiches
4 ounces Gouda cheese, freshly grated (about 1 1/2 packed cups)
steps: Position a rack in the center of the oven and preheat to 400°F. Line a sheet pan with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine the fennel, dill, vinegar, a generous pinch of salt, and a few cracks of pepper. Toss to quickly "pickle" and set aside.
Set the squash cut-side down on the lined sheet pan and roast until fork-tender, 30 to 45 minutes.

When the squash is cool enough to handle, peel off the skin and mash it with a potato masher, fork, or spoon until it resembles mashed potatoes — it won't be completely smooth. Don't discard any excess liquid.

Set a large Dutch oven over medium heat and melt 1 tablespoon of the butter. Add the garlic, rosemary, thyme, and sage and stir until fragrant, 30 to 45 seconds. Add the butternut squash, season with the paprika, nutmeg, cayenne, and a pinch of salt, and stir. Add about one-third of the grated cheese, 1 tablespoon of the butter, and the cream (quantity not visible in the photographed page — add to taste). Cook over medium-low, stirring constantly, until the butter and cheese melt together into a stringy mash. Add another one-third of the cheese and stir until melted, then add the remaining cheese and stir until melted in. Season to taste with additional salt and pepper and remove from heat.

recipes.title: Quick Dill Pickles
ingredients: Handful of fresh dill (or 2 Tbsp dried)
steps: In a small saucepan over medium-high heat, combine the vinegar, water, and salt. Let the salt dissolve.
Split the spices, garlic, dill, and bay leaves between two pint jars.
Chop the cucumbers and pack the jars full.
Pour the boiling brine over the cucumbers and let sit for at least an hour, then enjoy.
Storage: keeps in the fridge for up to three months, or leave 1/2-inch headspace and process 10 minutes via water bath canning for shelf storage.

recipes.title: Copycat Mateo's Gourmet Salsa
steps: Place the half jalapeño in a food processor.
Pulse until finely chopped.
Add the fire-roasted tomatoes, cilantro, garlic granules, cumin, red wine vinegar, lemon juice, and salt.
Pulse a few times until blended to a light, slightly chunky consistency.
Chill in the fridge for 30 minutes before serving to let the flavors mix.

recipes.title: Salmon with Cucumber Dill Sauce
ingredients: Dill oil (optional): 1/2 cup chopped fresh dill, plus sprigs for garnish
Dill oil (optional): 1 cup neutral oil (sunflower, canola, or grapeseed)
4 thick salmon, trout, or similar fish fillets
2-4 tablespoons clarified butter, walnut oil, or vegetable oil
2 tablespoons walnut oil or vegetable oil
Salt and a pinch of sugar
steps: Prepare the dill oil (optional): blend the oil and dill on high for one minute. Strain through cheesecloth into a bowl and refrigerate for gradual dripping. Can be made up to 3 days ahead.
Season the salmon: salt the fish pieces and refrigerate.
Cook the onions: gently cook the minced onion in walnut oil over medium-low heat in a covered pan until soft and translucent, avoiding browning. Puree and set aside.

Prepare the cucumbers: slice each lengthwise and scrape out the seeds with a spoon. Puree the unpeeled cucumber (with seeds) in a blender. Strain through a fine-mesh strainer into a bowl for 2 hours, undisturbed. Dice the peeled cucumber separately.

Make the sauce: whisk the strained cucumber liquid into the pureed onions until it reaches a melted-ice-cream consistency. Add 2 tablespoons of dill oil and season with lemon juice, salt, and white pepper. Serve at room temperature or gently warmed.

Sear the salmon: heat oil in a pan over high heat until nearly smoking. Pat the salmon dry and sear for 6-8 minutes on one side for a crispy crust. If very thick, flip and finish cooking; if under one inch thick, baste the exposed side with hot oil.

Plate: toss the diced cucumber and cherry tomatoes in the sauce. Pour into shallow bowls or plates with wells. Top with the salmon, seared-side up. Garnish with additional dill and salmon caviar if desired.

recipes.title: Salmon Risotto
ingredients: 1/2 cup minced shallots or yellow onion
2 cups risotto rice (Arborio, Carnaroli, or Vialone Nano)
6 cups salmon stock or low-sodium chicken stock
steps: Heat butter in a medium pot over medium-high heat. Add the minced shallots and saute until soft. Add the rice and stir well, cooking a few minutes before adding the Marsala or white wine. Stir constantly until the liquid mostly evaporates.

Add stock 1 cup at a time, stirring well. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook, stirring frequently, until each addition is mostly absorbed. Repeat until the rice is tender but slightly al dente, adding water if needed.

Once the rice reaches the desired consistency, stir in the salmon and pesto. Cook a few minutes longer. Adjust consistency with water as needed for a loose, bowl-ready texture. Season with pepper and serve.

recipes.title: Salmon Piccata
ingredients: 1 shallot, minced, or 1/4 cup minced onion
steps: Salt the salmon and let rest while prepping vegetables. Heat olive oil in a saute pan over medium-high heat. Pat the salmon dry and place skin-side down in the hot pan.
Sear until the flesh turns opaque, basting with hot oil, about 5 minutes. Test readiness by gently jiggling the pan.
For thick portions, flip and cook 1-2 minutes on the other side. Thin portions need no flipping.
Transfer the cooked fish, crispy side up, to a cutting board and add black pepper.
Add 1 tablespoon butter and the shallots to the pan; cook 1 minute. Add capers and lemon zest, cook 30 seconds, then add the white wine, scraping up browned bits with a wooden spoon.
Add the lemon juice and parsley. Reduce heat to low. Incorporate the remaining butter one tablespoon at a time, swirling until fully incorporated. Do not boil.
Serve the sauce over the fish.

recipes.title: Japanese Salmon Rice
ingredients: 1 3/4 cups salmon stock or dashi (or water)
steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl with water three times until the water runs mostly clear. Drain in a strainer while preparing the green onions and flaking the salmon.
Combine the rice, sake, and stock in a pot. Cover and bring to a boil on high heat. Reduce to medium-low and cook 10-15 minutes until the rice is mostly done.
Quickly uncover, add the green onions and salmon, then re-cover. Let rest 5 minutes.
Fluff the rice with the sesame oil and furikake seasoning before serving.

recipes.title: Salmon Stock
ingredients: 4 to 6 pounds salmon heads and bones
1 large white or yellow onion, chopped
steps: Cut the bones to fit into a large pot. Add the heads, bay leaves, and chopped vegetables. Cover with water by one inch. Set over medium-high heat and bring just barely to a simmer, about 15 minutes. Let steep at steaming point for 15-30 minutes only.
Turn off the heat. Strain through a fine-mesh strainer into a large bowl, keeping the fat. Discard the solids.

Pour the broth back into the cleaned pot. Add the dried kelp and heat to medium. Bring just to a simmer over about 30 minutes. The moment it simmers, turn off the heat and remove the kelp. Add salt to taste and serve.

recipes.title: Salmon Patties with Crackers
ingredients: Grated zest and juice of 1 lemon
Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Combine the salmon, green onions, mayonnaise, egg, salt, hot sauce, Old Bay, Worcestershire, mustard, lemon zest, lemon juice, and garlic in a bowl.
Prepare the horseradish cream by mixing the sour cream, horseradish, and milk; adjust consistency as needed for drizzling.
Heat oil to 325-350°F in a heavy skillet, about 1 inch deep.
Incorporate the crushed Saltines into the salmon mixture (starting with 1/4 cup, adding more as needed for cohesion). Form patties with moistened hands.
Combine the remaining crushed Saltines with the Wondra flour for coating.
Coat the formed patties in the flour mixture and fry until golden on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve with salad and the horseradish cream.

recipes.title: Shrimp Risotto
ingredients: 2 cups risotto rice (Arborio, Vialone Nano, Carnaroli, or Bomba)
A large pinch of saffron, crumbled
1/2 pound peeled shrimp, in small pieces
steps: Warm the shrimp stock in a small pot.

Heat the first 2 tablespoons of butter in a medium pot over medium-high heat. Add the shallot and rice; saute, stirring often, until translucent, about 4-6 minutes. Add the garlic and cook another minute.
Pour in the white wine and stir. Add 2 ladles of shrimp stock and the saffron.
Stir frequently, allowing the rice to absorb the stock. Add additional ladles before the rice sticks to the pot. Continue for 20-25 minutes until the rice reaches an al dente texture.
Stir in the shrimp, peas, parsley, and another ladle of stock. Cook until the shrimp are cooked through, about 3-5 minutes.
Turn off the heat and add stock or water to achieve a porridge-like consistency. Stir in the butter and black pepper. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Wild Game Liver Creme Caramel
ingredients: 3-4 pieces dried porcini or morel mushroom, crushed
Garnish: cherries, raspberries, or blackberries; dried figs soaked in balsamic vinegar; fried lardo, bacon, or pancetta; wild arugula or watercress
steps: Heat the sugar in a small pot over low heat until melted. Add the honey and red wine vinegar; stir well.
Paint the caramel into the bottom and sides of ramekins. Preheat the oven to 325°F.
Puree the liver and egg in a food processor, using pulses to avoid creating froth.
Heat the milk, cream, soy sauce, sugar, mushroom pieces, and quatre epices in a pot over medium heat until boiling slowly.
Temper the liver-egg mixture by slowly drizzling in the cream mixture while stirring (4-5 times), then pour the liver mixture into the cream.
Strain through a fine-meshed sieve.
Pour hot tap water into a casserole dish to halfway level.
Fill the ramekins with the mixture, leaving room at the top.
Cover with foil and bake in the water bath for 45 minutes; the custard should be set but wobbly.
Remove from the water bath and cool, covered, for 30 minutes.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
To serve, run a knife around the edges and invert onto a plate; the caramel pools around the custard.
Garnish with crispy, sweet, tart, and bitter elements.

recipes.title: Grilled Venison Heart with Peppers and Onions
ingredients: 1 or 2 deer hearts, or 1 elk, moose, or beef heart
1 tablespoon sherry or red wine vinegar
3 or 4 colored bell peppers, cut into 2-3 pieces each
1 large onion, cut into large wedges
steps: Trim the hearts by removing visible fat from the top and slicing along the natural gaps into thick cutlets. Remove the vein-like structures from the interior walls. Mix 2 tablespoons olive oil with the vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, salt, oregano, thyme, and pepper. Massage the marinade into the meat, place in a container, and marinate 30 minutes to 2 days.
Heat the grill to high. Coat the peppers and onions in the remaining olive oil and season with salt.
Place the hearts and vegetables on the grill with the pepper skin-side down. Leave uncovered for 8 minutes without moving them.
Flip everything and grill uncovered for 5 more minutes.
Check the vegetables for char and remove to foil to steam. Peel any blackened pepper skin.
If the hearts need more cooking, cover the grill and cook 2-5 more minutes until internal temperature reaches 130°F.
Tent the hearts loosely with foil and rest 5-10 minutes before slicing. Season with black pepper and sea salt at the table.

ingredients: 1/2 pound fresh salmon or trout, skin and bones removed
1/2 pound smoked salmon or trout, skin and bones removed
1/4 cup sour cream or creme fraiche
3 to 5 tablespoons unsalted butter, at room temperature
About 1 tablespoon prepared horseradish, or to taste

steps: Bring about one quart of salted water to a boil. Add the fresh salmon and turn off the heat. Cover the pot and let sit for 15 minutes. Remove the salmon and flake into a large bowl when cool enough to handle.

Break up the smoked salmon and add to the bowl along with the sour cream, 3 tablespoons butter, lemon juice, lemon zest, and chives. Use a heavy fork to mash together into a rough spread. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons butter if needed for consistency.
Season with salt, pepper, and horseradish to taste. Cover and refrigerate for about an hour before serving. Top with pickled mustard seeds or caviar if desired.

recipes.title: Corned Venison
steps: Combine all ingredients except the roast in a pot; bring to a boil. Cover, remove from heat, and cool to room temperature (several hours). Meanwhile, trim silverskin from the roast. Once the brine cools, place the meat in a container, submerge completely using a clean stone as a weight, and refrigerate for 5-7 days.

After the brining period, rinse the meat thoroughly. Place the roast in a pot with fresh water, just enough to cover. Partially cover and simmer gently — do not boil — for 3-5 hours until the connective tissue softens.
Serve hot or cold with mustard and sauerkraut. Store the finished product in its cooking broth in the refrigerator to maintain moisture, or freeze separately for up to one year.
